extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, inventors, and law students working with U.S. patent practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal rules for preparing and construing the patent specification and accompanying materials (drawings, models, specimens) under U.S. law, and related rules for patent extension and assignment interpretation. Focuses on statutory requisites, evidentiary/formal requirements, and how courts/juries construe specifications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification statutory requisites (Act of July 4, 1836, §6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before receiving a patent the inventor must deliver a written description of the invention or discovery, and of the manner and process of making, constructing, using and compounding the same, in such full, clear, and exact terms, avoiding unnecessary prolixity, as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to which it appertains ...; and in case of any machine, he shall fully explain the principle and the several modes in which he has contemplated the application of that principle ...; and shall particularly specify and point out the part, improvement, or combination, which he claims as his own invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an enabling disclosure sufficient for a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention; avoid unnecessary prolixity; for machines explain the principle and contemplated modes of application; expressly point out what is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification formal accompaniments (1836 Act continuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall be accompanied with a drawing or drawings and written references where the nature of the case admits of drawings, or with specimens of ingredients and composition of matter sufficient in quantity for experiment where applicable; descriptions and drawings must be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses and filed in the patent office; furnish a model where cases admit of representation by model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide drawings and written references whenever appropriate; for chemical/composition inventions provide specimens sufficient for experiment; sign and have two witnesses attest; file the specification and exhibits in the patent office; provide a model when required/appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification requisites under earlier law (Act of 1793)
rubrics_metrics.description: The earlier Act (1793) required a written description in such full, clear and exact terms as to distinguish the invention from all others before known and to enable any person skilled in the art to make, compound, and use the same; in case of machines fully explain the principle and several modes of application; accompany with drawings or specimens where applicable; description signed and attested by two witnesses; deliver model if Secretary deemed necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirms continuity of enablement, distinctness from prior art, requirement to explain principle/modes, and formalities (signatures, witnesses, possible model).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification is part of the patent and controls its construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Under U.S. practice the specification is drawn up and filed before the patent and a copy is annexed and referred to in the patent; the patent and the specification are to be construed together to ascertain the subject-matter of the invention, and the specification may control or limit the generality of the terms of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the specification with awareness that its language and drawings will be read with the patent itself and may restrict broad claim language; don't rely on the patent text alone—the specification and drawings will be used in construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of drawings in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings annexed to a specification, in compliance with the statute, form part of it and are to be regarded in construction; drawings not referred to in the specification may nevertheless be used to explain it, provided they accompany the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear drawings and reference them; drawings can be used to interpret ambiguous text but must be properly appended to the specification to have effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's role in construing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the province of the court to determine what is intended to be patented and whether the patent is valid in law; whether the invention is described with reasonable certainty is a question of law for the court upon construction of the patent terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate judicial construction issues: the court will resolve legal questions of claim scope and sufficiency of the written description/enablement; draft to minimize ambiguity that could generate adverse legal rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury's role and conditional construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury must take the construction of the patent from the court absolutely where there are no terms of art requiring explanation and no surrounding circumstances to be ascertained; where terms of art or surrounding circumstances affect meaning, the court gives a conditional construction and the jury determines the relevant facts and applies them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that factual disputes about the meaning of technical terms or the surrounding circumstances will be resolved by the jury applying the court's conditional instructions; include clear definitions and factual context in the specification to reduce jury-driven ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title/description requirement (Act of 1836, §5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall contain a short description or title of the invention or discovery, correctly indicating its nature and design, and referring to the specification for particulars, a copy of which shall be annexed to the patent specifying what the patentee claims as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, accurate title that reflects the invention and points readers to the full specification for details; ensure claims are clearly identified in the annexed specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment formalities and remedies (11th and 14th sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be assignable in law either as to the whole interest or any undivided part by an instrument in writing which, and also every grant and conveyance of the exclusive right under any patent, shall be recorded in the patent office; the fourteenth section authorizes suits to be brought in the name of the assignee or grantee for infringement of his rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execute assignments in writing and record them in the Patent Office to perfect legal title and enable assignees to sue for infringement; consider recording to separate assignee interests from the patentee's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant/extension of patent is a new grant of exclusive rights (effect of 18th section)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension of the patent under the eighteenth section is a new grant of the exclusive right or monopoly in the subject of the invention for the seven years; the patentee becomes reinvested with the exclusive right to make, use, and vend the thing patented, subject to the qualifying clause protecting certain users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that an extension vests exclusive rights anew in the patentee; evaluate how the renewal interacts with existing users and purchasers and whether any statutory qualification preserves limited usage rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory criteria and procedure to obtain extension (18th section procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute provides for application to a commission for an extension of the patent for seven years; the board hears and decides the application and, if the patentee's receipts and expenditures showing loss and profits establish to the satisfaction of the board that the patentee, without fault, failed to obtain a reasonable remuneration for his time, ingenuity and expense, the commissioners shall extend the patent for seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To seek extension prepare full accounts of receipts and expenditures demonstrating inadequate remuneration through use/sale, and apply timely to the commission before patent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of extension clause regarding assignees/grantees (right to use vs exclusive rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: The clause 'the benefit of such renewal shall extend to assignees and grantees of the right to use the thing patented, to the extent of their respective interests therein' is construed to refer to persons in the use of the patented machine(s) at the time of the renewal (purchasers/users) and to preserve their right to use to the extent of their interests, but does not in terms confer an exclusive right to make and vend (a monopoly) on assignees and grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not read 'right to use' as automatically creating exclusive rights to make/sell for assignees; statutory language and context should be used to avoid creating unintended monopolies—explicit formulae ('full and exclusive right of making, using, and vending') are needed to grant exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding harsh or unjust constructions; statutory interpretation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Where words or phraseology are obscure or doubtful, the intention of the lawmakers is to be sought from the context and general policy of the law; courts should prefer constructions that reconcile doubtful language with the overall policy and avoid consequences fraught with unmixed evil or unjust results unless compelled by express language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft clear, explicit statutory or contract language if a drafter intends to produce significant rights (e.g., assign exclusive monopolies); litigants and judges should interpret ambiguous clauses in light of legislative purpose and to avoid harsh/inconsistent results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraint for extension applications (no extension after expiration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute provides that no extension of the patent shall be granted after the expiration of the term for which it was originally issued; the extension must be granted before expiration to avoid injustice to purchasers who obtained the patented article after the monopoly expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File extension applications in good time, before patent expiration, to prevent leaving purchasers/users unprotected or exposed to later reinstated exclusivity without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and limits of contingent interests in extended term
rubrics_metrics.description: Contingent interests in the new term that derive from provisions in assignments under the old term rest upon contract, and the clause does not create such contingent interests but may change their legal character after the contingency occurs (possibly converting a contractual contingency into a vested legal right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting assignments that 'look to' an extension, include explicit provisions clarifying whether contingent extended-term interests become vested and how they are to be handled; recognize that absent clear language the contract governs the contingent interest.
